analysis: The PR is documentation-only: docs/provider/cli-reference.md adds one env-var table row (patch hunk at head line ~1687) documenting DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP (source ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift, shapeWarmupEnvironmentKey; '0' disables load-time shape warmup, 'always' skips shader-cache probe). The supplied units (head lines 1-846) are surrounding unchanged text, and the changed line itself falls outside the supplied excerpt. I examined the patch excerpt and surrounding documentation against the threat model, including the logout/token handling (A-008, T-053), cache settings (T-041), and attestation/Autopilot docs (TB-011). No security control, authorization, encryption, attestation, token custody or cache behavior is changed by the doc edit. The documented variable concerns performance warmup and does not touch prefix-cache keying, TTL, scope derivation or the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE gate. It is a daemon-forwarded environment variable, so the unreviewed Swift implementation (not supplied) should confirm that warmup uses no real consumer prompt data and does not alter cache or TTFT-oracle behavior (T-041, SEC-035). That is an unverified contract, not a finding. No threat-model updates are required from this change.
